title: Cooperate across a real difference in priorities

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Fair representation preserves the other position’s reason and accepted cost, not merely its preferred outcome. A cooperative arrangement can protect different goods without requiring shared beliefs.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Complete fictional statements. Alex: “A predictable Saturday lets me keep a 16:00 care handoff; I enjoy discovery but cannot return late.” Bea: “I want one unfamiliar experience; repeating the same cafe feels limiting, but I do not need an all-day trip.” Options: familiar cafe 13:00–14:00; new nearby exhibition 13:00–14:30 plus 30-minute return; distant outing returning 16:30. Both may decline; no booking is made.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Represent both voices, ask one useful clarification and propose a shared option with its remaining cost. Save the proposal before reading the clarification.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: One person wants quiet conversation; another wants a crowded concert. Is saying “you both really want entertainment” adequate representation?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Later clarification: Alex welcomes an unfamiliar venue if home by 15:30; Bea prefers the exhibition but accepts a private no-photo visit. Nearby exhibition returns 15:00 and fits both; distant outing does not. Cafe remains feasible but does not serve Bea’s stated exploration preference as well. Partial: fit the clock while calling Alex afraid of novelty. Incorrect: invent agreement to stay late. No real consent or visit occurred.
criteria: Both reasons and constraints are represented

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. It erases the different desired experiences. Ask about an actually welcome quieter shared time or separate participation; no arrangement must manufacture identical values or force agreement.
criteria: Both reasons and constraints are represented
